claims.statement: URE reported issuing 1,330 energy-efficiency certificates in 2025 with a combined value of 195,851.216 toe and an indicated aggregate property-rights value of about PLN 434m.
Poland's consolidated Energy Efficiency Act states that property rights arising from energy-efficiency certificates are exchange commodities, transferable through the certificate register.
Hypothesis: a partner-led aggregator can profitably recover certificate value from smaller, standardized projects; median award size, cycle time and attach rate remain unvalidated.

contrary_evidence: URE's reported aggregate certificate value does not establish the attainable value or profitability of the smaller projects targeted here.
Rights arise and transfer through the statutory register; a private pre-project contract cannot substitute for eligibility, issuance or compliant market transfer.

economics.acquisition_route: Recruit five installers in two repeatable project categories and retrospectively screen only future, not already-started, jobs; test ten dossiers before building software.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated path: at 400 processed projects per year and PLN 10,000 average net service revenue, annual revenue would be PLN 4m; 30% operating profit and a 5x operating-profit value imply PLN 6m enterprise value and PLN 4.8m for an 80% founder stake, with more than PLN 0.2m of previously distributed personal cash required to cross PLN 5m without counting retained earnings twice. A 7-9 year route requires installer density and automation evidence.
economics.founder_time: 10-15 hours per week for screening logic, partner coordination and exception review; qualified auditors and market intermediaries perform regulated or credentialed work.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated estimate: 45-65% after independent auditor, legal/registry and licensed-broker costs; margin depends heavily on batching similar projects and rejecting uneconomic files early.
economics.payback: Unvalidated target: 9-18 months, depending on URE timing; early screening fees should cover operating cost because success proceeds may arrive slowly.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: PLN 1,000-3,000 screening/audit coordination plus 20-35% of net realized certificate value; never quote a certificate value before audit and market confirmation.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Installers can feed every eligible quote and multi-site owners can repeat annually; retention follows recovered net proceeds and application reliability.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: an installer-embedded pipeline, project-type eligibility templates and observed URE outcomes lower acquisition and processing cost while exclusive mandates prevent cherry-picking after approval
fingerprint.customer: Polish SMEs, housing entities and installers planning repeatable energy-efficiency upgrades too small to justify an in-house certificate process
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: white-label the intake inside quotes from regional HVAC, industrial-maintenance and renewable installers, beginning with the family company's supplier and customer graph
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: eligibility screen, audit orchestration, application evidence pack, status tracking and compliant monetization, sold on a success-fee basis with no guaranteed award
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: the project owner pays a modest screening fee and 20-35% of net certificate proceeds only after issuance and sale; alternatively the service exercises a pre-agreed purchase option after issuance
fingerprint.problem_trigger: a qualifying upgrade is about to be ordered and the owner risks permanently missing a tradable support value because the application and audit were not prepared in time

founder_fit: Strong match to energy analytics, financial modeling and the parents' installation-business channel.
Can start with forms, rules and specialist partners rather than capital-intensive project ownership.
Success pricing creates an evidence-based sales story and minimizes continuous public-facing promotion.
AI can assist document extraction and completeness checks while final eligibility remains human-controlled.
risks: Applications can be delayed, rejected or yield less value than expected.
Commodity-market, brokerage, audit or legal activities may require partners or permissions the startup does not possess.
Small projects may not produce enough certificate value to support acquisition and expert costs.
Installers may submit incomplete files or begin work before the required process is in place.

structure.control_point: exclusive pre-project application mandates and contractually defined post-issuance purchase or monetization rights across an installer-sourced pipeline
structure.critical_dependency: projects must be screened before execution, satisfy statutory energy-savings rules, survive audit and URE review, and be monetizable through a compliant registry or brokerage route

thesis: Embed a white-certificate recovery workflow into HVAC, compressed-air, motor, heat-recovery and building-upgrade installers. Before eligible work begins, the project owner grants an exclusive application mandate and a post-issuance sale option or revenue-share agreement; the service coordinates an independent audit, URE paperwork and sale through an appropriately authorized market participant. The wedge is recovering value from subscale projects that owners and installers would otherwise ignore, without promising eligibility or buying certificates before issuance.
title: White-Certificate Recovery Desk for Small Efficiency Projects
uncertainties: Which two project types have the best ratio of repeatability, certificate value and audit cost?
Can a lawful post-issuance purchase option and success-fee structure be standardized for target owners?
What is the real median time from application to tradable rights?
Will installers accept an exclusive embedded mandate rather than refer clients to existing consultants?
